commits.subject: fix(localsandbox): harden command classification, pathguard, and env sanitization
fix(localsandbox): bound post-kill pipe drain, session-scope file approvals, and harden adapter and skilltree

invariants_checked: Service.Run enforces shipped ApprovalMode only (ModeAuto, ModeAsk), resolves WorkDir through PathGuard.CheckDir (O_NOFOLLOW directory walk), serialises concurrent operations per workspace root via ref-counted rootLocks while running approval prompts outside the root lock, and masks secret assignments in command preview logs.

Process lifecycle kills the child process group on timeout or context cancellation, stops watchKill before PID reuse, caps captured stdout/stderr streams at 1 MiB per stream, and closes pipe readers after a 100ms post-kill grace window so escaped setsid() descendants cannot hang drain(proc).
FileApproval binds out-of-scope file writes to both the SHA-256 content digest and the originating SessionID, and readForChange rejects non-regular files via Lstat before reading.
Session state (grants, delete rules, approval mode overrides) is keyed per sessionID, mutex-protected under -race, and released cleanly on ReleaseSession; zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: watchKill signalled proc.Kill() on timeout/cancel without closing stdout/stderr reader pipes after a post-kill grace period, allowing an escaped setsid() grandchild holding inherited stdout/stderr descriptors open to hang drain(proc) and hold the workspace root lock indefinitely.
FileApproval lacked SessionID binding and readForChange did not reject non-regular files (symlinks, FIFOs, devices) via Lstat before opening target paths during AuthorizeFileChange.

invariants_checked: Adapter bounds all host file store operations (EnsureSessionDir, ListSessionFiles, StatSessionFile, ReadSessionFile, WriteSessionWorkspaceFile) through PathGuard and workspace root locks, refuses DestroySession and VersionsWorkspace on user host folders, and enforces FileApproval session + SHA-256 digest binding.

StatSessionFile and ListSessionFiles (and InstallManager.StatSessionFile) classify regular files, directories, and non-regular entries (symlinks, FIFOs, sockets, devices) identically to remote sandbox adapters (RemoteEntryOther) and honor ctx.Err() cancellation.

InstallManager isolates maintenance sessions per bound skill version directory, never implements SessionCapabilityProvider (preventing chat agents from reaching an open-network shell), and redirects UV/PIP/npm caches and GENYEE_SKILL_DIR inside .genyee/cache; zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: Adapter.guard and Adapter.WriteSessionWorkspaceFile trusted fileApprovalFrom(ctx) without verifying approval.SessionID == sessionID, allowing an out-of-scope FileApproval context from one session to grant read/write access in another session.

Adapter.StatSessionFile, Adapter.ListSessionFiles, and InstallManager.StatSessionFile classified symlinks and special files as RemoteEntryFile instead of RemoteEntryOther, and ListSessionFiles ignored ctx.Err() during WalkDir traversal.

invariants_checked: PolicyBuilder and Escalation protect credential roots (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, ~/Library/Keychains, appData, .bsk), shell startup files, system/root directories, home dot-directories, and .git metadata (including worktrees and bare repos with HEAD+objects+refs), resolving symlinks on longest existing prefixes before granting access.

PathGuard enforces lexical and symlink-resolved DenyRead, DenyWrite, ReadOnlySubpaths, WritableRoots, and WritableFiles, walks relative components fd-by-fd on Unix with O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC and O_NONBLOCK leaf opens, verifies S_IFREG before reading/truncating, and caps ReadFile at 64 MiB.

BuildCommandEnv and FilterInheritedEnv allowlist safe locale/toolchain host variables, strip dynamic-linker injection (LD_*, DYLD_*), runtime startup hooks (NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONSTARTUP, RUBYOPT, PERL5OPT, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV, ENV, PROMPT_COMMAND, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, etc.) case-insensitively, reject '=' and NUL smuggling in keys/values, and force GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.

Command delete classification covers rm/rmdir/unlink, find (-delete/-exec rm, BSD/GNU pre-path flags, symlink-following -L/-H/-follow), git (clean/rm with -C, -C<dir>, --work-tree, --git-dir, and escaping pathspecs), shell -c, eval, substitutions, and env/sudo wrappers (-C/-D/--chdir, env -S/--split-string); zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: ClassifyCommand, DeleteLocations, and DeletesStayBelow missed attached/long git directory options (-C<dir>, --work-tree, --git-dir), git rm/clean pathspecs escaping cwd, BSD/GNU find pre-path flags (-L, -H, -P, -f <path>) and symlink-following (-L, -H, -follow), and wrapper chdir/split-string forms (env -C, sudo -D, env -S, --split-string), allowing destructive out-of-cwd or root/home deletes to bypass dangerous-command refusal or ModeAuto review.

PathGuard.allowWrite (used by WriteFile and MkdirAll) omitted g.writeDenied(path) (Policy.DenyWrite), NewPathGuard did not resolve symlink aliases on DenyRead, DenyWrite, and ReadOnlySubpaths, and Policy/PathGuard accepted NUL bytes in path strings.

PathGuard.ReadFile and WriteFile opened leaf files without O_NONBLOCK and without verifying S_IFREG (allowing workspace FIFOs to block goroutines forever in openat while holding workspace locks, or writes to non-regular files), and ReadFile used unbounded io.ReadAll.

BuildCommandEnv matched blockedExplicitEnv case-sensitively, allowed '=' and NUL bytes in explicit env keys/values (enabling KEY=VAL smuggling past exact-name blocklist lookup when flattened by EnvSlice), and did not normalize mixed-case Windows Path.

invariants_checked: Seatbelt compiler never interpolates paths directly into SBPL source: every dynamic path is passed out-of-band via sandbox-exec -D KEY=VALUE parameters and referenced through (param "..."), eliminating quote/parenthesis/newline SBPL injection.

resolvePolicyPaths canonicalizes WritableRoots, ReadOnlySubpaths, WritableFiles, ReadableRoots, PrivateRoots, DenyRead, DenyWrite, and Cwd via EvalSymlinks on longest existing prefixes so macOS /var -> /private/var and /tmp -> /private/tmp symlinks match kernel path evaluation.

Base SBPL profile denies default operations, restricts network unless NetworkUnrestricted, confines file-write* to parameterized writable roots/files, carves out PrivateRoots/DenyRead, DenyWrite, ReadOnlySubpaths, and .git metadata (last-rule-wins), hardcodes /usr/bin/sandbox-exec, spawns with Setpgid: true, and redirects TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP to Cwd.

findings.summary: seatbeltProcess.Kill unlocked p.mu prior to syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL) (leaving a race window with Wait reaping pid) and lacked a post-kill pipe close fallback for escaped setsid() descendants, and withSandboxTemp stripped inherited TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP case-sensitively.

invariants_checked: Skill names are restricted to single non-dot path segments without slashes or NUL bytes, preventing traversal outside <root> or collisions with .versions, .locks, and .next-* bookkeeping entries.

Version directories live immutably under <root>/.versions/<name>-<n>, Activate atomically swaps <root>/.next-<name> onto <root>/<name>, Discard and Prune verify version ownership before RemoveAll, and Sweep skips skills locked by active installers.

Advisory locks open <root>/.locks/<name>.lock with O_NOFOLLOW on Unix and enforce process-local mutual exclusion on non-Unix platforms, with idempotent sync.Once unlock functions; zero weknora/wk_ residues.

findings.summary: validName permitted dot-prefixed names (.versions, .locks, .next-*), New checked clean == string(filepath.Separator) instead of filepath.Dir(clean) == clean (missing Windows drive roots), Sweep returned an error on malformed .next- symlinks instead of removing them, lock_unix.go omitted O_NOFOLLOW/sync.Once, and lock_other.go was a no-op that broke tryLock exclusivity on non-Unix.

invariants_checked: Windows stub backend compiles cleanly under GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 and fails closed with core.ErrUnsupportedPlatform across Available, EnsureReady, Prepare, and Spawn, never falling back to unsandboxed host command execution.
